item.research_question: How does the partial substitution of non-magnetic Mg2+ with magnetic Co2+ in Y-type Ba2Mg2Fe12O22 hexaferrites affect the crystal structure, iron oxidation state, and magnetic phase transition temperatures?
item.processing_route: Sonochemical co-precipitation: metal nitrates dissolved in deionized water with 10 wt% over-stoichiometric Ba(NO3)2, precipitated with NaOH at pH = 11.5, sonicated with 750 W ultrasound (40% amplitude) for 15 min, dried, milled, calcined at 700 °C, and heat-treated at 1170 °C for 7 hours in air.
item.test_conditions: XRD at ambient temperature (40 kV, 30 mA, Cu-Kα); Mössbauer spectroscopy at room temperature (±12 mm/s velocity range); Magnetization measurements at 4.2 K and 300 K up to 50 kOe; ZFC/FC curves in fields of 50, 100, 500, and 1000 Oe from 4.2 to 300 K.
key_findings: The material is an almost pure Y-type hexaferrite phase with only 1.4% CoFe2O4 impurity.
Unit cell parameters remained unchanged compared to unsubstituted Ba2Mg2Fe12O22 (a = 5.8613(1) Å, c = 43.503(1) Å).
Isomer shifts of 0.27–0.38 mm/s confirm high-spin Fe3+ with no ferrous Fe2+ observed.
Magnetization at 50 kOe increased to 34.5 emu/g at 4.2 K and 30.5 emu/g at 300 K.
Two magnetic phase transitions were observed, both shifted to higher temperatures compared to the undoped compound.
The ferrimagnetic-to-helical spin order transition occurs at approximately 195 K (depending on field).
A second transition to a longitudinal-conical spin state was determined at 85 K (at 500 Oe).
The coercive field at 300 K was found to be about 35 Oe.
item.mechanism: The substitution of Mg2+ by Co2+ in octahedral sites does not alter the iron oxidation state but modifies the magnetic anisotropy, which is temperature and field-dependent, thereby shifting the magnetic phase transition temperatures to higher values and increasing saturation magnetization.
item.limitations: The authors state that the reason for the decrease in the second transition temperature to 78 K at 1 kOe is still unknown.
item.future_work: The authors propose future studies using structure-sensitive methods, including neutron diffraction, combined with other advanced techniques to prove multiferroicity, especially given the transition temperatures are now above liquid nitrogen temperature.
quotes: The magnetization values at 50 kOe were 34.5 emu/g at 4.2 K and 30.5 emu/g at 300 K.
The ferrimagnetic arrangement at room temperature is transformed to a helical spin order at about 195 K, which is considered to be a prerequisite for the material to exhibit multiferroic properties.
The reason for this decrease is still unknown.
